...give them wine to observe their decorum, and place them in diverse situations to observe their composure <term>se</term> <gloss>facial expression and internal state</gloss>. Through these nine tests, even the most unworthy person can be fully understood. 

Zheng Kaofu <margin>A member of the ducal clan of the State of Song and the tenth-generation ancestor of Confucius</margin> was stooped <margin>A scholar <note>the first rank of officialdom</note></margin> <margin>A stooped back</margin> when first appointed, bowed further when appointed a second time <margin>A Great Officer <note>the second rank</note></margin>, and bent low <margin>His body was hunched as he did not dare take up space on the road</margin> when appointed a third time. <margin>Such was the genealogical record of Kaofu</margin> <margin>Who would dare not take this as a model?</margin> <margin>Nine men <note>referring to a group or a specific count in the commentary</note></margin> When he received a command, he would bow and walk along the wall. Who would dare not follow such a disciplined path? 

But as for those common men, upon their first appointment <margin>Word technique</margin> they become haughty <margin>An appearance of pride and arrogance</margin>; <margin>Word technique</margin> upon their second appointment <margin>Word technique</margin> they dance atop their carriages <margin>Riding in a carriage with a boastful, swaying manner</margin>; <margin>Word technique</margin> and upon their third appointment <margin>Word technique</margin> they address their uncles by their personal names. <margin>Calling his elders by their names</margin> 

How great was the yielding virtue of Xu You <margin>How great was the yielding virtue of Xu You in ancient times!</margin> in the past! To have a conscious intention to be virtuous is the thief of virtue <margin>To have a mind set on being virtuous is the enemy of true virtue</margin>. And when the heart is enslaved to what is right before the eyes <note>literally: between the eyebrows and eyelashes</note>, virtue becomes even more of a fabrication <margin>When the mind is occupied with superficial appearances, virtue is further corrupted</margin>. 

Because of this, if one looks back into the heart <margin>Sentence structure</margin>, one finds constant agitation and confusion <margin>From this, looking inward at the heart, all is in turmoil, making it impossible to achieve virtue or progress in the Way</margin>; in the end, one can neither complete virtue nor advance toward the Way. <margin>Eye, ear, nose, tongue, heart</margin> <margin>Heart</margin> 

<unclear>協</unclear> There is no greater thief than a virtue that possesses a conscious heart, and a heart that possesses "eyelashes" <note>meaning a heart that looks outward or is concerned with how it is seen by others</note>. When one is clever, they look inward; yet by looking inward with a self-conscious mind, they are ruined. There are five types of harmful virtue, and the most dangerous is the virtue of the heart <note>referring to the ego-driven center of the self</note>.

<summary>This page contrasts the genuine humility of Zheng Kaofu, who became more modest with each promotion, against the arrogance of common men. It warns that conscious or performative virtue is a "thief" that prevents one from reaching the Way.</summary>

<keywords>Zheng Kaofu, humility, arrogance, Xu You, yielding virtue, nine tests of character, inner vision, Five Harmful Virtues</keywords>
